title: MokA: Multimodal Low-Rank Adaptation for MLLMs

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 (visual-text benchmarks), MME column, LLaMA2 + LoRA row
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 lists LLaMA2+LoRA MME as 90.85, but Tables 4 and 11 report the identical configuration as 908.52. Every other MME value in Table 2 falls in the 774-1292 range, so 90.85 is a dropped-digit corruption of 908.52.

Section 6 claims MokA 'completely solves the problem of multimodal adaptation' and 'absolutely ensures superior model performance,' yet Table 3 shows Uni-modal LoRA (36.80/36.50) and Uni LoRA + MM LoRA (37.10/37.60) both beat MokA (35.40/36.70) on LLaMA2 speech-text, and the Abstract itself hedges that 'gains vary among backbones and modalities, suggesting further exploration is needed.'

The Abstract says 'gains vary among backbones and modalities, suggesting further exploration is needed to fully assess its generality and robustness,' while Section 6 declares MokA 'completely solves the problem' and paves the way for 'final, conclusive exploration of multimodal-aware adaptation.' The hedged framing and the absolutist conclusion are mutually contradictory.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 5 (ablation) vs Table 3 (speech-text), AIR-Bench column, LLaMA2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For LLaMA2 on AIR-Bench, Table 5 reports Multiple LoRA = 31.97 and MokA = 39.64, while Table 3 reports 32.80 and 36.70 for the identical configurations. Only the shared LoRA baseline (31.75) agrees across the two tables, isolating the discrepancy to the affected rows.

Text claims 'Qwen2.5-VL with LoRA outperforms both LLaMA-2 and Qwen2,' but Table 1 shows Qwen2.5-VL LoRA MUSIC-AVQA (73.00) is below LLaMA2 (73.41), and Qwen2.5-VL LoRA AVE (71.38) is below Qwen2 (72.13). The immediately following frozen-visual-connector explanation only makes sense if Qwen2.5-VL is underperforming, so the claim is inverted.

The core cross-attention equations in Section 2.2.2 are normalized by 1/sqrt(d) (d = projection dimensionality), but Appendix B reproduces them with 1/sqrt(N_t) (text token count) while claiming 'the notation is consistent with the main manuscript.' Attention logits must be scaled by sqrt of the feature/key dimension, not the sequence length, so the appendix version is mathematically mis-scaled and inconsistent with the main text.

Text states DoRA [21] 'focuses solely on optimizing the gradient direction.' DoRA (Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation, ICML 2024) actually decomposes the pretrained weight into magnitude and direction components and learns both via a LoRA-style update on the direction component; it does not focus solely on the gradient direction. The attribution is a mischaracterization of the cited work.

Equation 13 writes the cross-modal text contribution as B*0_{N_t}, with 0_{N_t} defined as 'the zero vector of dimension N_t' (the text token count). Since B is in R^{d x r}, B can only multiply a vector in R^r; the zero term should be of the rank r (or output) dimension, not the token count N_t. The stated dimensionality is inconsistent even though the term evaluates to zero.

Text claims 'multiple LoRA ... underperforms both standard LoRA and MokA.' On LLaMA2 AVE, Multiple LoRA (71.77) exceeds standard LoRA (69.84), so the claim only holds on MUSIC-AVQA, not on AVE. The categorical 'underperforms both' statement is contradicted by the paper's own Table 1.

summary: Verified in uncertainty mode (uncertainty threshold 0.30, lenient strictness). The paper was segmented into 75 snippets (30 sections/appendices, 16 equations, 13 tables, 14 figures, 2 code blocks). Triage scored every snippet; 41 high-uncertainty snippets (uncertainty >= 0.30) were routed to specialist verifiers (math, text, statistical, citation, vision) and the remaining 34 low-risk snippets were recorded as NO_ERROR at confidence 1.0 - uncertainty. A whole-paper cross-section pass was also run. 9 findings survived filtering (math/statistics >= 0.70, text/citation >= 0.70, vision >= 0.75 under lenient strictness), including 3 high-confidence (>= 0.85) errors: (1) the LLaMA2+LoRA MME value in Table 2 (90.85) contradicts the identical configuration reported as 908.52 in Tables 4 and 11; (2) the absolutist Discussion ('completely solves ... absolutely ensures superior performance') contradicts both the hedged Abstract and Table 3, where two baselines beat MokA on LLaMA2 speech-text; (3) the Abstract's 'further exploration is needed' directly conflicts with the Discussion's 'final, conclusive exploration.' Additional findings: Table 5 and Table 3 disagree on LLaMA2 AIR-Bench for Multiple LoRA and MokA; Section 4.1 inverts the Qwen2.5-VL comparison against Table 1; Appendix B re-scales the cross-attention equations by sqrt(N_t) instead of the main text's sqrt(d); DoRA is mischaracterized in Related Works; and Equation 13's B*0_{N_t} term has an inconsistent dimensionality. Figures could not be pixel-verified (no image files are present in the workspace); captions were checked against the text and are consistent. A ground_truth.json exists in the paper directory but findings were derived independently from the paper's own internal evidence.
